title: Downed wires & electrical hazards
label: ELECTRICAL HAZARDS
deck: Keep away from fallen wires, damaged electrical equipment and anything touching them, including water, fences and vehicles. Assume wires are live even when they are quiet or the neighbourhood has no power. Do not attempt a rescue by touching a person or object in contact with electricity. Contact the utility or emergency services from a safe place.
tldr: Keep away from fallen wires, damaged electrical equipment and anything touching them, including water, fences and vehicles. Assume wires are live even when they are quiet or the neighbourhood has no power. Do not attempt a rescue by touching a person or object in contact with electricity. Contact the utility or emergency services from a safe place.
steps: Do not approach to determine whether a wire is live. Current can travel through wet ground and conductive objects. Keep others and animals away.
Do not touch fences, trees, vehicles or debris that may contact a wire. Do not use a stick or tool to move it.
Stay out of flooded electrical areas
Never enter water to reach a breaker, appliance or person near damaged electrical systems. Use qualified help.
Tell people to avoid the area from your safe location. Report a clear location without approaching for a photograph.
Leave flooded, scorched or broken equipment off until qualified personnel assess it. A restored grid does not make damaged wiring safe.
next: If a wire falls onto a vehicle you occupy, generally stay inside and call for help; fire or another immediate threat changes the decision. Follow qualified emergency instructions rather than touching the vehicle and ground together.
